Definition: from κόλος (dwarf); properly, to curtail, i.e. (figuratively) to chastise (or reserve for infliction):--punish.
BiblicalUsage: Kolazo means to punish, to chastise, to reserve for infliction. Acts 4:21 says the council let Peter and John go, finding nothing how they might punish them, because the people glorified God, and 2 Peter 2:9 says the Lord knoweth how to deliver the godly out of temptations, and to reserve the unjust unto the day of judgment to be punished.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Acts 4:21 and 2 Peter 2:9 show both hands of God: He delivers the godly and reserves the unjust, and the council that could not punish the apostles learned that the Lord can.
